correctness.rationale: For every n≥2 the primitive rays of the face fan of Q_n are v_{p,q}, p≠q, with entries −(2n−1),1,2 and sum zero. If a Demazure root existed, the sum of ray pairings zero combined with one pairing −1 and all other pairings nonnegative forces exactly one +1 and all other 0. For n≥3, there are two rows of zero pairings; their complementary coordinate restrictions force all character coefficients equal, a contradiction. For n=2, the six distinct ray directions show any four rays span rank two; no nonzero character vanishes on four. Hence Aut0=T by the established complete-toric root-subgroup theorem. Any fan automorphism preserves Q_n and its facets; lower facet has n rays, upper n(n−1). For n≥3 the counts differ; n=2 has two equal-size facet types but respective cone lattice determinant indices 3 and 8 separate them. Permuting lower facets forces the entire integral fan automorphism to be the corresponding coordinate permutation, so Aut(N,Σ)=S_{n+1}. As Aut0=T is characteristic in the full automorphism group, all automorphisms normalize it, giving T⋊S_{n+1}. Independently computed ray rank upon deletion of any two rays for n=2..6 and the index-3/index-8 boundary, corroboration of the all-n argument.

value.rationale: The full automorphism group is a fundamental structural invariant of a newly introduced infinite family of singular toric Q-Fano varieties, relevant to equivariant geometry, moduli and symmetry classification. Computing its unipotent-root absence and every component is a motivated family-specific theorem, not a restatement of the generic toric automorphism classification; the n=2 exceptional facet ambiguity is treated nontrivially.
